subject.title: OpenClaw local embedded Ollama/Qwen session fails live-data request that Pi coding agent handles via shell/curl

question: After confirming current behavior, should OpenClaw stop at policy-preserving direct exec visibility, or should it guarantee additional automatic live-data-to-shell routing for lean local models?
rationale: The merged repair intentionally restores permitted exec visibility without adding aliases, routing heuristics, or a permission bypass; deciding whether OpenClaw should go further changes the model-facing tool and security policy rather than merely fixing a mechanical regression.

options.title: Keep the narrow visibility contract
options.body: Confirm the reported flow on current main and close this issue if the model can select permitted exec; track any concrete wrapper argument defect separately.

options.title: Define an explicit local-model fallback policy
options.body: Sponsor a scoped design for automatic live-data routing only if maintainers want that behavior despite its shell and network policy implications.

recommendation.title: Keep the narrow visibility contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the reported flow on current main and close this issue if the model can select permitted exec; track any concrete wrapper argument defect separately.
